Udnie (Young American Girl, The Dance)

Francis Picabia, 1913

Oil on canvas

Fragmented, interlocking planes in grey, black, blue and green, close to abstraction.

Use this style

Francis Picabia, Udnie (Young American Girl, The Dance), 1913. Centre Pompidou, Paris. Source on Wikimedia Commons. Licence: Public domain.

About the painting

Picabia painted Udnie in Paris in 1913 after a trip to New York for the Armory Show. On the crossing he had watched the dancer Stacia Napierkowska perform, and the painting turns that memory into a whirl of interlocking shapes. It is a very large canvas, about three metres square, and was shown at the Salon d'Automne the same year. It is now in the Centre Pompidou in Paris.

Nothing in it is a recognisable body any more. Curved and angular planes in grey, black, white, blue and green overlap as if seen from several angles at once, close to Cubism and to Robert Delaunay's Orphism, and right at the edge of abstraction.

How it looks on your photo

One of the strongest styles. Photos break into sharp grey, white and blue facets with flashes of green. Bold shapes and architecture take it well. At full intensity the subject can disappear, so lower the intensity if you want to keep it recognisable.
